claims.text_en: The merged unit is anchored by BTS Sala Daeng station (code S2, Silom Line, opened 5 December 1999, five exits, on Si Lom Road southwest of the Sala Daeng intersection) and MRT Si Lom station (code BL26, opened 3 July 2004, beneath Rama IV Road at the Sala Daeng intersection, reported as the Blue Line's deepest at about 30 metres), connected to each other by a covered elevated walkway.

geography.place_name: BTS Sala Daeng (S2) and MRT Si Lom (BL26)
geography.notes: both stations define the unit; app merges stops ~330 m apart, and the two Wikipedia coordinate centroids (13.7285/100.5341 vs 13.7292/100.5375) sit roughly 300-400 m apart

temporal_scope.notes: opening years are historical; station geometry stable

evidence.paraphrase: S2 Silom Line station in Bang Rak on Si Lom Road SW of the intersection, opened 5 Dec 1999, five exits on the U2 floor with an MRT connection, coordinates 13.7285083N 100.5341333E

BL26 opened 3 Jul 2004 beneath Rama IV at the Sala Daeng intersection; described as the deepest Blue Line station (~30 m) with a long escalator; linked to Sala Daeng BTS via a covered elevated walkway; coordinates 13.7292N 100.5375E

limitations: depth and escalator claims are encyclopedic, not operator-verified
the ~330 m app merge distance is app data, not independently measured here

claims.text_en: MRT Si Lom's Exit 1 sits on the northeast corner of the Sala Daeng intersection near a Lumphini Park entrance, and the park's southwest corner lies at that intersection, with the 57.6-hectare park stretching northeast between Ratchadamri and Witthayu roads along Rama IV.

question_answers.notes: Aliases: Sala Daeng (ศาลาแดง), Si Lom/Silom (สีลม); administrative: Silom/Suriyawong sub-districts of Bang Rak khet (BTS S2 is in Bang Rak; Lumphini park sits in Pathum Wan). Physical stops: BTS Sala Daeng S2 (1999) and MRT Si Lom BL26 (2004), ~300-400 m apart by coordinate centroids, covered walkway link. Named corridors inside: Silom Road frontage, Soi Sala Daeng, Soi Convent, Patpong Soi 1-2, Soi Thaniya (per Wikipedia Patpong), Silom Soi 5. Inside: both stations, Silom Complex, Central Park mall (Silom-Rama IV corner), Lalai Sap (Soi 5), Patpong. Partial: Lumphini Park (western/southwestern edge only). Outside: One Bangkok (opened 2024-10-25, east of the park per Khaosod context) and most of Surawong Road. All membership calls except the stations and intersection-corner sites rest on the app's 800 m nearest-stop catchment and must be confirmed against the app polygon by the coordinator.

The distinctive everyday experience is the office-worker day: weekday lunch markets (Lalai Sap, Convent carts, Soi 10 courts) priced for people on a break, described across 2023-2026 guides. The experience belongs to Silom's office population on weekdays; tourists take over the Patpong strip after ~17:00.

Value mechanisms: dual-line interchange at one intersection (c01), cheap weekday food variety steps from desks (c04, c05), anchor groceries/retail with direct BTS access (c12), park-edge access (c14). Guide opinion vs fact: the food claims are observation-backed (three independent guides); the interchange and retail claims are factual; park access strength is factual for the edge but partial for the unit.

Deliberate counter-evidence: documented Patpong inflated-bill scams and Thailand-wide FCDO spiking warning (c10); guides advise avoiding the Patpong side and call it unfit for children (c11); the interchange requires an above-ground, exit-and-walkway transfer with a ~30 m deep MRT platform (c18); rents sit at the top of asking ranges (c08). Weekend users lose the area's signature markets (c04).

Day: office markets to ~15:30, malls to ~22:00, park 04:30-21:00. Night: Patpong market ~17:00-24:00 alongside go-go bars; Commons Saladaeng DJ nights, liveliest Fri/Sat. Weekday vs weekend: the office markets shut down weekends; no dedicated weekend survey found (limitation inside c17). Season: not covered in this pass; not_found for seasonal variation.

Walk-to-transit reality: five BTS exits, MRT exits on both intersection corners, a covered elevated walkway between the lines, street-level bus stops, and a mall (Silom Complex) with a direct BTS connection. Distances stated, not durations: building listed 290 m from BL26; Lalai Sap ~0.5 km west of BTS Sala Daeng; MRT exit 1 beside the park entrance. No walking times were derived from the app radius; the interchange's above-ground nature means transfer time depends on escalators/crowds, unmeasured here.

Groceries: TOPS supermarket at Silom Complex B level (c12); Central Park mall adds a Tops Food Hall and 70 street-food stalls per Khaosod (c15). Ordinary food: Lalai Sap + Convent/Sala Daeng clusters (c04, c05). Healthcare: King Chulalongkorn Memorial Hospital adjacent to the stations (c13). Gyms: Lumphini's pool/sporting ground/jogging paths sit at the park (c14) but only its edge is inside the unit; condo gyms and a fitness-club inventory inside the unit were not verified this pass - partial.

Asking rents only - no signed-lease data found (period limitation: 'early 2025' for the median figure, portal listings Dec 2025-Jan 2026). Sample limits: one building's 19 listings read in full (c06); platform ranges without methodology (c07). Conclusion: app 38k/60k matches top-of-range station-adjacent asking prices, not the ~22-28k 1BR median band (c08, inference).

What is actually inside: the park's southwestern corner and the entrance by MRT Si Lom Exit 1 (c02); the 57.6 ha, 2.5 km of jogging paths, lake and pool belong to the whole park and only its edge falls in the catchment (c14, partial). Tree cover vs access: the unit itself is dense CBD blocks; green access is park-edge access, plus the new free rooftop park (11,200 sqm, opened 2025-09-03) at the intersection (c15). App's green hectares must be re-derived from the polygon intersection.

Conditional fit: strong for CBD professionals/expats/digital nomads who can pay the station-adjacent rent premium and want weekday food variety and dual-line transit (c08, c05); weak for families seeking quiet evenings (Patpong strip adjacency; c11) and for weekend-centric lifestyles (markets close; c17). No universal 'best-area' framing used; guide-sourced fit statements only.

Operating changes: Central Park mall opened 2025-09-04 and rooftop park 2025-09-03 (c15; One Bangkok opened 2024-10-25 nearby but outside the unit, per Khaosod context). Regulatory: BMA approved Convent Road as a formal vending zone on 2025-12-24 (c16). Also noted but not claim-grade here: Wikipedia reports BMA announced a Lumphini Park hawker centre along Ratchadamri Road (announced Aug 2025, 'opening early 2026') - single-source, recheck before use. Event vs publication dates distinguished in each claim's temporal_scope.

Uncertainties: asking-vs-signed rent gap unknown (c08); scam recency rests on a 2016 account plus non-citable review platforms, FCDO warnings are Thailand-wide (c10); Lalai Sap's western end may fall nearer Chong Nonsi than Sala Daeng (c03); park hectares inside the unit need polygon derivation (c02). Outside-the-score: the brief's 'Duangtawee/monkey-pool' tension could not be verified in reliable public sources (adult-venue directories rejected); Patpong Museum reported closed May 2023, status unverified; Silom Edge (opened 2022, former Robinson site) mentioned by Khaosod but not polygon-checked.

editorial.preview: A dual-line CBD interchange where weekday office markets and a 57.6-hectare park edge sit a few hundred metres from a 1967-founded go-go strip that turns into a night bazaar at 17:00.
editorial.guide_lead: Sala Daeng / Si Lom is a merged BTS-plus-MRT unit at the Sala Daeng intersection in Bang Rak's financial district, with the two stations linked by a covered elevated walkway rather than an in-fare transfer. Its everyday food story is a weekday one: Lalai Sap in Silom Soi 5 (Monday-Friday, roughly 06:00-15:30) and the Convent Road carts serve office-priced plates steps from the platforms, then close on weekends when malls and the park carry the day. The Patpong sois flip the same streets after dark into a market-and-go-go strip with a documented inflated-bill economy around upstairs show venues. Lumphini Park's southwestern corner and an entrance by MRT Si Lom's exit put a 57.6-hectare park within the unit's reach, though most of the park lies beyond it. Rent is the sore point: station-adjacent towers ask at the top of the range while guide medians for one-beds sit around 22,000-28,000 baht.

strengths.text_en: Two rail lines meet at one intersection - BTS Sala Daeng (S2) and MRT Si Lom (BL26) on either side of it, joined by a covered walkway - giving the unit a dual-line interchange few Bangkok blocks have.

Weekday-only, office-priced food markets sit inside the unit: Lalai Sap (Mon-Fri, ~06:00-15:30) in Silom Soi 5 and the Convent Road carts that Travelfish calls the street-food highlight of the Sala Daeng area.
Everyday retail is anchored at the doorstep: Silom Complex connects directly to the BTS station and carries a TOPS supermarket and a four-floor Central department store.
Park access is real, not just tree cover: Lumphini's southwestern corner with its lake, jogging paths and public pool touches the unit near MRT Si Lom's Exit 1.

The 4 September 2025 opening of Central Park mall - with a food zone of 70 street-food stalls and Michelin-listed venues plus a free 7-rai rooftop park opened 3 September - added day-to-night food and elevated green at the intersection.

tradeoffs.text_en: The app's rent references (38k one-bed / 60k two-bed) match the top of observed asking ranges in station-adjacent towers, well above the ~22k-28k one-bed median band guides cite for the area.

The nightlife engine carries an externality: Patpong's show-venue inflated-bill pattern is documented (quoted 200-baht drinks becoming a 3,800-baht bill in one 2016 account), and the UK FCDO warns of drink spiking in tourist areas across Thailand - a national warning, not Patpong-specific.
Crowd pressure is concentrated, not ambient: Lalai Sap's narrow lanes peak hardest around weekday lunch with limited seating, and the same office flow drives intersection-level congestion.
The interchange is above-ground: the MRT platform sits ~30 m down and the BTS-MRT link runs through exits and walkways, so transfer effort depends on crowds rather than platform adjacency.

day_night.text_en: Weekday day: office-worker markets to mid-afternoon, mall food courts and the park from early morning; Patpong's sidewalks are ordinary CBD frontage.
Evening: Patpong market runs ~17:00-24:00 alongside the go-go bars; The Commons Saladaeng turns DJ-led and is liveliest on Friday and Saturday nights.
Weekend: Lalai Sap and the Convent carts shut; malls (Silom Complex, Central Park) and Lumphini's edge carry the day, and the park keeps 04:30-21:00 hours.

within_area_variation.text_en: Patpong Soi 1-2 (bars, market, touts) and the Convent Road/Lalai Sap food lanes sit roughly 100-200 m apart but draw different crowds; guides point eaters to the food lanes and steer them off the Patpong side.

Rent varies block by block: a 2005 tower on Soi Sala Daeng 2 (listed 290 m from BL26) asks 24k-40k for one-beds, while district guides put the median band at 22k-28k and sois toward Surawong below the core.
Green is edge-loaded: the park's southwestern corner and one entrance fall by the MRT exit, while most of the 57.6 ha stretches northeast beyond the unit.
Lalai Sap sits toward the unit's western end near the Silom-Naradhiwas junction, about half a kilometre west of Sala Daeng BTS - its nearest stop may be Chong Nonsi for parts of the soi.

conditional_fit.text_en: Strong fit for CBD professionals, expats and digital nomads who want dual-line transit and weekday food variety and can absorb the station-adjacent rent premium.
Poor fit for families wanting quiet evenings: Patpong's adult strip abuts the main nightlife zone, and a resident guide explicitly advises against it for children.
Weak fit for weekend-centric routines: the signature markets close Saturday-Sunday, leaving malls and the park edge as the weekend offer.
Park users should price the edge, not the brochure: real lake-and-pool access exists, but only the park's western slice is inside the unit.

uncertainties: All rent figures are asking prices; no signed-lease data was found, so the app's 38k/60k blend cannot be validated against achieved rents.

Patpong scam documentation is strongest from a 2016 first-person account; 2024-2026 reports exist on review/social platforms that are not stably citable, and no news article on a recent Patpong case surfaced.
The UK FCDO drink-spiking warning applies to tourist areas across Thailand and does not name Patpong; local incident statistics were not found in this pass.
The brief's 'Duangtawee/monkey-pool vs patron safety' tension could not be verified in reliable public sources; adult-venue directory sites surfaced and were rejected.
Which park hectares and which Lalai Sap blocks fall inside the app polygon must be checked by the coordinator; this research used coordinate geometry and source-stated distances only.
Lumphini Park hawker centre (announced Aug 2025, 'early 2026' opening per Wikipedia) and Patpong Museum's reported May-2023 closure are single-source and need rechecking.
Nightlife-10 attribution: Patpong's market-plus-bars mix is confirmed as the visible engine (c09), but the app's score weighting to the scam externality remains an editorial judgment.

open_issues: Rent blend decision: app one_bed=38,000/two_bed=60,000 aligns with premium station-adjacent asking stock, not the ~22-28k 1BR median band; coordinator should decide whether rent references should blend medians or keep the premium blend (c07, c08).

Polygon checks owed by coordinator: Lumphini Park share inside the 800 m catchment; Lalai Sap inclusion and which stretch of Convent Road (right side) is inside; Silom Soi 9-Sathon 12 and Surawong inbound vending-zone edges (c02, c03, c16).
